newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end flat on late blue chips rebound.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end flat on late blue chips rebound.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed Tuesday a fraction firmer after a late spurt of blue chip buying recouped early declines, brokers said.
"Core blue chips including KEPCO rebounded before the close on the back of active buying by onshore funds," said fund manager Ahn Hyo-moon of Korea Investment Trust Co.
The composite stock index rose 0.07 points to 694.97, off the day's low of 687.87.
"The market will remain solid as the consolidation shown today was smaller than expected," said analyst Kim Wan-hee of Dongsuh Securities.

Brokers said investors remained positive about an economic turnaround, given steadily rising prices of semiconductors, steel products and petrochemical goods, which are the nation's major export items.
"I'm not quite sure whether the economy has hit rock bottom but I believe the worst is over for the economy," Ahn said. He added the won/dollar rate would be a variable for the economy.
Brokers said advanced buying ahead of an increase in the foreign stock ownership ceiling on May 2 also boosted blue chips.
KEPCO rose 200 won to 26,900 and POSCO gained 200 won to 54,000.

Chipmakers briefly hit yearly highs in early trading on anticipation that a recent recovery in memory chip prices would help improve their earnings. Samsung Electronics expects the unit price for 16-megabit DRAM chips to rebound to $13-$14 in the second quarter from around $9 in the first quarter.
Samsung rose 400 won to end at 64,200 after peaking at 65,000. LG Semicon and Hyundai Electronics closed the day at 29,700 won and 40,500 won respectively, off highs of 30,600 and 41,600.
Ahn forecast the index would reach the 800 level in the second quarter. -- Yeom Yoon-jeong (822) 727 5647
